    Who these estimates are for

    Women aged 65–89 diagnosed with stage I–III invasive breast cancer in Ontario between 2010 and 2017, with known ER, PR, HER2, grade, T and N (18,873 women, followed to the end of 2022). The estimates are less reliable for combinations that were rare in this group, such as T4 or N3 tumours, or a Charlson score of 4 or more (under 2% of women).

    How the estimates are made

    Three competing-risk models were fitted to the same variables: T, N, ER, PR, HER2, grade, age, 4-year Charlson score group (0, 1, 2 or more), trastuzumab, anthracyclines and radiotherapy. "Cox" is a cause-specific Cox model, "Forest" a random survival forest and "DeepHit" a neural network. Each gives the chance of dying from breast cancer, cardiovascular disease, another cancer, or any other cause, with the remainder alive.

    Reading the results carefully

    • Treatment options show outcomes among women who did or did not receive that treatment. Healthier women were more likely to be treated, so differences partly reflect who was chosen for treatment, not only the effect of treatment.
    • The Charlson score is worked out from the conditions you tick, using the original Charlson weights, and then placed in a group: 0, 1, or 2 or more.
    • Estimates have not been validated outside Ontario. They support, and do not replace, clinical judgement. For research use.
